still trying to get into the first dark souls game, any advice?

Souls games are amazing you can start with any of them. However they are challenging and may seriously enrage you during your first gameplay. With that said, you can choose from 5 titles and you will not be disappointed with any of them:

  • Demon's Souls (DeS for short): PS3 only. The original "Souls" game, dated and rough for the current standards however it defined the entire saga. My personal favorite.

  • Dark Souls (DS for short): PS3, XBox and PC. Refined several aspects of DeS and with a completely new story. A flawed gem but a good starting point. The PC port has some serious issues that I'm not sure if they were ever fixed.

  • Dark Souls 2: PS3, PS4, Xbox, Xbox1 and PC. Refined even more aspects of the previous game but for some this is the "black sheep" of the saga. However, for some people it's their favorite Souls game.

  • Bloodborne: PS4 exclusive. Different story and settings yet remains a Souls game at heart. With that said Its style is far more aggressive.

  • Dark Souls 3: PS4, Xbox and PC. Arguably the best Souls game released, it refined the aspects of the previous games while bringing new most welcome stuff.

You can play the games in any order, however, I highly recommend to play DS3 AFTER finishing DS1 since they are heavily connected. (But is not required, you can enjoy the game without any knowledge of the first one). DS2's story is not that connected to the other games. DeS and Bloodborne have independent stories.

Now some general advice:

Get a good controller if you plan to play on PC. Preferably a PS/Xbox one, the game is not designed for keyboard and mouse.

Be patient and cautious. NEVER EVER play mad. This is probably the best advice anyone can give you.

You will die, a lot. You will lose your currency. You will be invaded and easily killed by other players. All of this is part of the experience, you will cherish it once the game finally "clicks" for you.

Most of the time you can only blame yourself for getting killed.

Summoning people to help you will make the game much more easier.

Always try to fight enemies 1 on 1. You can use a bow to aggro individual enemies at a safe distance.

Never underestimate an enemy.

Always explore. Outside of the useful stuff you will find, there is usually a shortcut to the boss somewhere. (No need to repeat the whole level)

Your initial class and gears are not that important.

A good shield (100% physical absorption) will do wonders at the beginning. With time you will learn to time your evasions and even parry.

Fat rolls are a no no... unless you know what you are doing.

Study your enemies, some enemies are easy to backstab, others is just better to let them attack, so you can safely block and counterattack. Some enemies are harder to fight and you will need to understand their patterns to defeat them without taking damage.

Always read the messages left by other players, many times they will guide you to secrets and stuff. But be careful and pay attention, not all messages are well intended.

Some specific recommendations depend on what game you are getting into.

In general you will enjoy the game far more if you play it without following a guide. However, feel free to use one once you cleared the game the first time. There is a lot to discover!

And finally, the Souls games are not perfect they have some annoying flaws specific to each game or shared among all of them. However, in their imperfection they offer you something missing in most modern games.

Don't try to go for a jack of all trades builds.

Pick an idea and stick with it for a while. Melee builds are consistently good throughout each title and IMO the best part of the series so I would heavily advise picking a melee build.

If you want to hit slow and hard pick str. If you want to be nimble and fast pick dex.
